economics.assumptions-describe.0003.all: Consumers spend their limited income (JD 51) on the combination of goods/services giving the greatest total satisfaction/utility; they compare the benefit from each purchase.

economics.assumptions-explain.0004.all: Rohan has limited income (€46) so cannot buy both maybe; compares satisfaction/utility expected from book vs jeans relative to price; chooses the one giving most satisfaction per euro; opportunity cost is the item forgone.

economics.assumptions-state.0011.all: Workers aim to maximise their wages/earnings (rewards from work).

economics.bop-analyse-1.0002.all: Causes: high consumer incomes/spending on imports (electronics, cars) - high income elasticity of demand for imports; fall in export competitiveness of manufacturing (higher costs, strong exchange rate, low productivity) so exports fall; X-M falls so deficit widens; chain to current account 5.2% of GDP.

economics.bop-analyse-2.0006.all: Benefits: injection into circular flow -> higher AD, output, employment (oil exports); foreign currency earnings/reserves; appreciation makes imports cheaper -> lower inflation, cheaper raw materials; improves living standards.

economics.bop-assess-1.0003.all: Consequences: leakage reduces AD -> lower growth, job losses in manufacturing; currency may depreciate -> imported inflation; borrowing/selling assets to finance. Evaluation: depends on cause (consumer boom vs capital imports), size 4.5% and persistence 10 years, how financed, depreciation may self-correct.

economics.bop-assess-2.0006.all: Good: injection, jobs in manufacturing, reserves. Not always: appreciation reduces future competitiveness, may be inflationary (excess AD), implies deficits elsewhere/protectionism, could mean low domestic consumption; depends on size/cause.

economics.bop-define1.0002.all: Part of the balance of payments recording trade in goods and services plus primary and secondary income flows.

economics.bop-define2.0007.all: Exports and imports of intangible products (e.g. tourism, banking, insurance, transport) between residents of one country and the rest of the world.

economics.bop-describe.0013.all: It may be short-term/temporary (e.g. importing capital goods/machinery that will raise future productive capacity and exports), so it will self-correct; or financed by inward investment.

economics.bop-explain.0005.all: Oil demand is price inelastic, so value of imports rises (spending on imports rises by large proportion as quantity barely falls); import expenditure increases relative to exports so current account deficit widens / surplus shrinks; also higher costs for exporters reduce competitiveness.

economics.bop-mcq-class.0002.all: Its banks providing insurance to foreign firms

economics.bop-mcq-def.0002.all: The part of the balance of payments that records trade in goods and services plus primary and secondary income flows

economics.bop-state.0008.all: Trade in goods (or trade in services / primary income / secondary income)

economics.competition-analyse-1.0004.all: Price wars risk: interdependence, if one cuts price others follow (kinked demand) so revenue falls; non-price competition (advertising, branding, coverage, contracts) builds brand loyalty, makes demand more price inelastic, raises market share without lowering prices; prices similar so differentiate; barriers to entry.

economics.competition-analyse-2.0002.all: Higher prices (price maker, no substitutes, consumer surplus lost); poor quality/service as no competitive pressure (x-inefficiency); lack of choice; less innovation; inelastic demand for water essential.

economics.competition-analyse-3.0002.all: Lower prices (online retailer low prices), more choice, convenience of next-day delivery, better quality/service as firms compete, innovation; but closure of 20% of shops reduces local choice.

economics.competition-assess-1.0001.all: Benefits: economies of scale -> lower costs/prices possibly, innovation from profits, advertising informs, non-price competition improves quality. Costs: similar prices suggest collusion/tacit, higher prices, advertising costs passed on, barriers. Depends on regulation, contestability.

economics.competition-assess-2.0001.all: For: lower prices, better service, efficiency, innovation, choice. Against: natural monopoly - economies of scale lost, duplication of pipes, profit motive may cut quality/safety, regulation alternative. Depends on regulation and infrastructure sharing.

economics.competition-assess-3.0003.all: Firms must cut costs/prices, lower profits, closures (14% shops), job losses; incentive to innovate, improve service, go online, efficiency; survivors may specialise/differentiate. Depends on firm's ability to adapt, niche products.

economics.competition-define1.0007.all: When firms agree to work together (e.g. fix prices/output) rather than compete.

economics.competition-define2.0002.all: A market dominated by a few large firms (high concentration ratio) that are interdependent.

economics.competition-describe.0017.all: Firms agree to fix prices higher than competitive level, so consumers pay more and lose consumer surplus/choice.

economics.competition-evaluate-1.0003.all: Benefits: economies of scale, investment/innovation, quality via non-price competition. Costs: similar prices -> tacit collusion, high prices, less choice, barriers; cement is homogeneous so advertising wasteful. Judgement depends on regulation/competition authority, contestability, imports.

economics.competition-evaluate-2.0004.all: For: lower fares, better service, efficiency, innovation. Against: natural monopoly, duplication, safety, loss of economies of scale, private firms may abandon unprofitable routes. Alternatives: regulation, franchising. Judgement.

economics.competition-evaluate-3.0006.all: Negative: lower prices/profits, closure 23%, job losses, high street decline. Positive: efficiency, innovation, adopt online, differentiate on service; online retailer gains. Depends on size, niche, time period.
